councils.name: City of Yarra
councils.visionStatement: By 2050, a robust, highly functional and multi-modal transport network in which it is easier, faster and safer for people of all ages and abilities to get around Yarra (Moving Forward: Yarra's Transport Strategy 2022-32).
strategicPriorities: Mode hierarchy that prioritises walking, cycling and scooters first, then public transport, then private vehicles
Deliver a connected, low-stress active transport network ('New Deal' walking and cycling programs)
Reduce traffic speeds and volumes on local streets
Improve public transport reliability, accessibility and capacity, including dedicated rights-of-way
Manage on-street parking to discourage car dependency
quantifiedTargets: Car trips through/within Yarra forecast to rise 48% on current trends if unaddressed — strategy aims to bend this curve down
86% community support (survey) for a lot more active and sustainable transport options
Bring the 39% of the cycling network that is currently non-compliant up to safety standard
councils.policyNarrative: Yarra's mode hierarchy places walking, cycling and micromobility above public transport and private cars, and the Council's Transport Strategy 2022-32 explicitly targets reduced car dependency and a step-change in active transport infrastructure. A GTP for this site should foreground secure, high-capacity end-of-trip cycling facilities, direct connections to the local bicycle network, and measures that actively discourage single-occupant car trips (e.g. unbundled/limited car parking, priority car-share bays).

councils.name: City of Melbourne
councils.visionStatement: A connected city where people and goods move efficiently through safe, liveable streets that prioritise walking, cycling and public transport over private vehicles (Transport Strategy 2030).
strategicPriorities: Expand unobstructed, tree-lined footpaths and convert 'Little' streets into pedestrian priority zones
Deliver 50km of protected bicycle lanes over 10 years
Reduce local road speed limits to 40km/h
Increase public transport capacity, reliability and signal priority
Manage kerbside space to prioritise deliveries, servicing and active/public transport over general parking
Support electric vehicles and zero-emissions transport, and regulate micromobility for public benefit
quantifiedTargets: 50% reduction in transport fatalities/serious injuries by 2030 (from 231 baseline)
Halve central-city through-traffic: from 43% to 21% of trips by 2030
Increase public transport/walking/cycling mode share from 64% to 70% by 2030
Increase the proportion of women cycling from 24% to 40%
councils.policyNarrative: The City of Melbourne's Transport Strategy 2030 sets an explicit mode-share target (70% of trips by public transport, walking or cycling by 2030) and a halving of central-city through-traffic. A GTP in the municipality should quantify how the development contributes toward these targets, prioritise high-quality end-of-trip facilities given the CBD's already-high public transport and active travel mode share, and align car parking provision with the Strategy's kerb-space and through-traffic reduction goals.

councils.name: City of Port Phillip
councils.visionStatement: A city that is connected and easy to move around — fitting more people into existing spaces while preserving community values (Move, Connect, Live: Integrated Transport Strategy 2018-28).
strategicPriorities: Safe, connected and convenient active transport choices
Public transport choices that make it easy to move and connect
Manage shared, limited on-street parking collaboratively across users
Support new transport options and technology
quantifiedTargets: No fixed mode-share targets published; strategy is framework-based with a 2024 mid-cycle review completed

sourceDocuments.title: Move, Connect, Live: Integrated Transport Strategy 2018-28

councils.policyNarrative: Port Phillip's Move, Connect, Live strategy is framed around fitting a growing population into a constrained street network, so on-street parking pressure and car-share/carpooling provision are a particular local sensitivity. A GTP here should give weight to car-share bay provision, resident parking permit interactions, and safe, connected active transport links given the coastal/foreshore trip generators nearby.

councils.name: City of Stonnington
councils.visionStatement: A shift from planning for vehicles to planning for people, recognising diverse travel needs across the community (draft Transport Strategy 2040).
strategicPriorities: Road safety — reduce crashes and improve safety for all travellers
Sustainable transport — increase walking, wheeling, riding and public transport use
Fair, consistent and transparent parking management
quantifiedTargets: Zero fatal and serious injury crashes on Council-managed roads by 2040
50% of trips made by walking, wheeling or riding by 2040
Retain roughly 1 in 7 parking spaces available at peak times in shopping centres
councils.policyNarrative: Stonnington's draft Transport Strategy 2040 targets 50% of trips by walking, wheeling or riding and zero serious-injury crashes, with lower local street speeds (≤40km/h) as a key lever. A GTP here should emphasise pedestrian safety and amenity (crossings, footpath quality) alongside cycling, and should note the strategy is still in draft/consultation — confirm final adopted targets before relying on the numbers above.

councils.name: City of Boroondara
councils.visionStatement: Safe, sustainable and connected transport, with a strong focus on reducing emissions from Council operations and the community (Climate Action Plan, Theme 4: Transport).
strategicPriorities: Reduce vehicle numbers and accelerate transition to electric/low-emission Council fleet
Expand cycling and walking networks — separated paths, improved crossings, links to transport hubs
Roll out EV and e-bike charging infrastructure
Support flexible/remote work to reduce commuter vehicle trips
Develop new Integrated Transport, Bicycle and Public Transport strategies (in progress)
quantifiedTargets: No numeric mode-share or trip-reduction targets published as at this profile's research date — directional actions only

sourceDocuments.title: Boroondara Climate Action Plan – Theme 4: Transport

councils.policyNarrative: Boroondara's Climate Action Plan and 2022 Bicycle Strategy put strong emphasis on separated cycling infrastructure, EV/e-bike charging, and flexible work to cut commuter trips. A GTP here should feature EV charging provision prominently and connect the site to the expanding separated bike path network, while noting Boroondara's new Integrated Transport/Public Transport strategies are still in development at the time of writing.

councils.name: Merri-bek City Council
councils.visionStatement: Mode shift away from private car dependency toward sustainable transport, underpinned by the Moreland (now Merri-bek) Integrated Transport Strategy 2019 and Zero Carbon Merri-bek Climate Emergency Action Plan.
strategicPriorities: Prioritise sustainable modes over private cars in the Integrated Transport Strategy
Expand parking restrictions in activity centres and remove minimum parking requirements for new development
Advocate for improved public transport frequency and reliability
School-based walking/cycling/scooting behaviour-change programs
Expand public EV charging and transition Council fleet to zero emissions
quantifiedTargets: 5km of new shared path construction (Council target)
Average Council light-vehicle fleet emissions below 100g/km CO2-e
Significant decrease in residents driving to work as sole drivers (directional, not numeric)
Electric vehicle ownership rate substantially above the Melbourne average (directional, not numeric)

sourceDocuments.title: Zero Carbon Merri-bek – Climate Emergency Action Plan 2020/21–24/25

councils.policyNarrative: Merri-bek has removed minimum parking requirements in activity centres and actively restricts on-street parking as a mode-shift lever, and its Climate Emergency Action Plan pushes EV charging and fleet transition. A GTP here should treat car parking minimisation and EV charging provision as high-priority items, and connect to the Council's shared path expansion program.
